title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (October 2026 data) — the one edition a year the publisher's own last-Tuesday rule places inside Christmas week
source: EST: derived from the publisher's own stated schedule rule, re-read direct from a primary today rather than carried. press.spglobal.com's June-2026-data release (2026-08-25-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-June-2026), fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 90,693 bytes), states it verbatim: `The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET.` December 2026's Tuesdays are the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th, so the last is 2026-12-29; the same release's two-month reporting lag (published 2026-08-25, reporting June data) puts October 2026 data on that edition. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED FROM A DISTRIBUTOR THIS CALENDAR HAD NOT USED BEFORE: prnewswire.com's Case-Shiller listing and per-item `datePublished` stamps, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (search HTTP 200, 220,741 bytes; eleven item pages HTTP 200, 265-271 KB each), record twelve consecutive realized editions from 2025-09-30 to 2026-08-25 — every one a last Tuesday of its month, including 2025-12-30, the last Tuesday of December 2025. Filed `estimate` on the same three counts the case-shiller-hpi-2026-10-27 entry documented: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs has no member for a private index provider's own standing publication rule, this lane never self-confirms, and the date is derived from a RULE rather than read off a publisher-posted December date. The St. Louis Fed's forward calendar for this release (fred.stlouisfed.org/releases/calendar?rid=199) — the second source the 2026-10-27 lane used, which named that date outright — returned HTTP 200 today but rendered NO release rows, and every fred.stlouisfed.org data endpoint timed out, so that corroboration could not be refreshed and is cited at its 2026-09-08 date rather than restated as current. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, after reading the single proposal that discovered it (from-treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28), which this file now shadows. It is the calendar's third Case-Shiller entry, and the first December one. WHAT IS TRUE OF THIS EDITION AND OF NO OTHER, and it is arithmetic rather than a base rate: the last Tuesday of December falls between the 25th and the 31st in EVERY year (verified 1990-2050), so the publisher's own rule places its December edition inside the Christmas-New Year week every single year, and December is the only month where that rule can collide with a market holiday at all — Dec 25 is the only fixed-date US market holiday that can ever fall on a last Tuesday. In 5 of the 37 years 1990-2026 (1990, 2001, 2007, 2012, 2018) the last Tuesday of December WAS Christmas Day. 2026 is not one of them: Dec 25 2026 is a Friday and 2026-12-29 is an ordinary full session. THE FINDING THAT QUALIFIES TWO SIBLING LEDGERS: eleven datable editions on PR Newswire carry a `datePublished` between 09:45 and 11:09 ET (median ~10:03), NONE before 09:30 — so the narrative release reaches the wire after the open and at roughly the same minute as Conference Board Consumer Confidence, which is the premise the case-shiller-hpi-2026-10-27 ledger's pre-open-gap design and the fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 ledger's 9:00-10:00 window kill switch both rest on. The 9:00 a.m. ET stamp is the publisher's stated INDEX publication time; it is not, on the wire record, when the headline arrives. Impact `low` and `symbols: []` inherited on the siblings' measured grounds and not re-argued: no macro- or housing-keyed house playbook exists (0 hits, re-grepped 2026-09-09), and the 2026-10-27 lane's nine-instrument pre-open test returned zero hits at p<0.05. Read-it-do-not-trade-it. An estimate widens caution; nothing here licenses an entry.
